newsitem.title: CHINA: China gives Vietnam murder suspects.
newsitem.headline: China gives Vietnam murder suspects.

text.p: Chinese police have repatriated two Vietnamese murder suspects in what appears to be a sign of warming ties between age-old adversaries Beijing and Hanoi.
Police in the southern province of Guangdong recently sent back to Vietnam two men suspected of murdering a Vietnamese woman in China in 1995, the People's Daily Overseas Edition said on Thursday.
The men ran a kidnapping ring that sold Vietnamese women in China and were wanted for other crimes in Vietnam, the newspaper said.
"Therefore the Vietnamese police raised the hope that China would repatriate the two criminals for handling by the Vietnam side," it said.
The repatriation follows moves to improve relations between Beijing and Hanoi, which have a history of border disputes and military clashes despite similar communist systems.

China and Vietnam crossed swords in a 1979 border war and their navies fought briefly in 1988 in the Spratlys, a potentially resource-rich island chain in the South China Sea. Border skirmishes continued into the early 1990s.
Relations have improved in recent years, but territorial tensions have continued to strain a rapprochement crowned by the normalisation of diplomatic relations in 1991.
Simmering differences flared last March, when a Chinese oil rig began exploratory drilling in a contested area of the South China Sea off the coast of central Vietnam.
Ties improved in July when Vietnam's Communist Party General Secretary Do Muoi visited Beijing and held talks with his Chinese counterpart, Jiang Zemin.
Soon after Muoi's visit, Vietnam said it had made progress in talks with China aimed at settling the oil rig row.
Both Beijing and Hanoi have appeared eager to ensure their improved relations are not derailed by territorial quarrels.
